title: Model Registry & Versioning
interviewAnswer: A model registry stores versioned model artifacts plus metadata, evaluation results and lifecycle state. It gives deployment systems an explicit, auditable model version to promote or roll back.
why: A model registry provides controlled versioning and lifecycle metadata between experimentation and deployment.
intuition: Think of it as a catalog of deployable model artifacts with versions, metrics, provenance and approval states—not just a folder of checkpoint files.
deepDive: A registry entry should reference model artifact, preprocessing/tokenizer, training run, data/code versions, evaluation results and stage/approval. Promotion should use automated and/or human gates. Rollback means redeploying a previous approved artifact/config, not retraining from memory. Multiple deployments can point to different versions during canary/shadow tests.
workedExample: Model v12 is “Production”; v13 passes offline metrics and becomes “Staging.” A canary detects latency/quality regression, so traffic returns to v12.
commonMistakes: Versioning only the weights but not preprocessing/tokenizer.
Promoting based only on one aggregate metric.
followUps: What metadata belongs with a model?
production: Use immutable artifact identifiers and deployment manifests so every prediction can be traced to an exact model/preprocessing version.

lab.goal: Represent model versions as immutable artifacts and implement a simple promotion/rollback pointer.

visual.title: Model registry lifecycle
visual.caption: A registry links each model version to metadata, evaluation and deployment status so releases are reproducible and reversible.
